title: Open restriction preserves module stalks after scalar transport
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf, $U\subseteq X$ open, and $x\in U$. Write $Y=X|_U$ and $y=(x,h)$, with restriction to the open subspace obtained from the slice-site equivalence [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The inverse of the canonical ring-stalk isomorphism $\rho:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ transports the $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-module stalk of $F|_U$ to an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. There exists an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear isomorphism from this transported module to $F_x$.

source.place: Tag 00A0, lemma-restrict (3), in Section 009Z; module scalar transport as in Modules Tag 01CP third paragraph.

proof.text: Take the linear component maps with their germ formula from new-module-restriction-stalk-components. Compare their underlying additive maps with the restriction-stalk isomorphism induced by the final neighborhood functor (Mathlib PresheafedSpace.restrictStalkIso). Equality on all germs gives equality on the colimit. The additive comparison is invertible and forgetting module structure reflects isomorphisms.

theorem nonempty_moduleRestrictionStalk_iso
    (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (F : Modules X) (U : Opens X) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U) :
    Nonempty
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
          (X.toPresheafedSpace.restrictStalkIso U.isOpenEmbedding ⟨x, hxU⟩).inv.hom).obj
        ((moduleStalkFunctor (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding) ⟨x, hxU⟩).obj
          ((U.sheafOfModulesEquivOver (moduleRings X)).functor.obj (F.over U))) ≅
        (moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj F)
